argument: Oum (arXiv:2607.16356v3, Sec. 9.3) states Conjecture 21 (Archdeacon; Jaeger: every bridgeless graph has an orientable 5-CDC, i.e. at most 5 Eulerian=even subgraphs, each with an Eulerian orientation, every edge used once in each direction), remarks it implies Tutte's 5-flow conjecture, and proves Lemma 22 (= Lemma 13.1.5 in Zhang's book): an orientable k-CDC gives a nowhere-zero Z_k-flow. Proof re-derived: pad to exactly k subgraphs C_1..C_k (so 'at most five' vs 'exactly five' is immaterial), fix a reference orientation, let chi_i be the signed characteristic vector of the directed Eulerian C_i (an integer circulation), and set phi = sum_i i*chi_i mod k. Each edge e lies in exactly two distinct C_i, C_j (an even subgraph contains an edge at most once) traversed in opposite directions, so phi(e) = ±(i-j) with 1 <= |i-j| <= 4, nonzero mod 5. Tutte's theorem (Z_k-flow iff integer k-flow) turns this into a nowhere-zero 5-flow. The BM hypothesis ('2-edge-connected') vs the target ('bridgeless') is bridged by working componentwise (flows are local to components; loops take any nonzero value and can be removed first), so the node statement exactly matches the lemma's hypothesis.
citations: arXiv:2607.16356v3 (S. Oum, A proof of the cycle double cover conjecture by OpenAI: an exposition), Section 9.3, Conjecture 21 and Lemma 22
C.-Q. Zhang, Integer Flows and Cycle Covers of Graphs, Lemma 13.1.5 (cited by Oum; not read directly)
